findings.evidence: plan.md now defines active/deleted receipt lifecycle, one tombstone transaction, retained Session/Memory/Provider/binding/handoff/receipt provenance, active-delivery plus active-owner list filtering, idempotent delete replay, terminal session_deleted response after deletion, no Session-ID reuse, and prohibition of generic ensure_session revival. Binding FKs use RESTRICT and ordinary delete cannot update or delete the immutable binding.
findings.root_cause: The revised plan makes DELETED terminal across visibility, ownership, routing, Provider and immutable provenance instead of partially reviving one Session identity.

findings.evidence: plan.md lines 269-271 order Sessions by last-message activity and Projects by last_opened_at, and place catalog_revision in every cursor. However lines 132-133 only require revision bumps for visible Project/Session create, delete, relocate and backfill completion. They do not cover message appends or last_opened_at updates, even though those mutate the cursor ordering keys. A message or selection between page requests can therefore move a row across the boundary without producing stale_cursor, causing duplicate or skipped Sessions despite the new keyset protocol.
findings.root_cause: The revision fence is not coupled to every mutation of the Project and Session ordering keys. The plan must either bump catalog_revision in the same transaction as message-activity and last_opened_at changes, or define a snapshot-watermark cursor whose ordering cannot change during traversal, and add interleaved-mutation pagination tests.

findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE/ARCHITECTURE.md section 3.3 now records v17-v31 migration ownership as the current fact. plan.md Task 8 adds an executable v31 prerequisite, a startup-blocking ProjectSessionUpgradeCoordinator, verified pre-v32 backup and manifest before DDL, durable phase/high-water/chunk/outcome state, transactionally advanced bindings/counters/cursor, completion conservation and digest gates, idempotent completed startup, guarded hash-checked restore with no down-migration, and crash injection before and after every schema/backfill boundary.
findings.root_cause: The revised plan gives schema installation and semantic conversion one fail-closed startup protocol with a backup lifetime, resumable checkpoints, completion oracle and explicit restore path.
